description: Baseline STRIDE rule base: 18 rules, 3 per category. Undeclared controls are treated as absent.

rules.title: Unauthenticated internet-facing entry point
rules.description: An application component reachable from the internet does not authenticate callers, so any party can impersonate a legitimate user.
remediation: Require authentication on every internet-facing route (e.g. Cognito authorizer on API Gateway).
Prefer token-based (OAuth 2.0 / OIDC) authentication over static credentials.

rules.title: Unauthenticated cross-boundary service call
rules.description: A service-to-service data flow crosses a trust boundary without the caller authenticating, allowing an attacker in the lower-trust zone to impersonate the calling service.
remediation: Authenticate service-to-service calls with IAM SigV4, mTLS or signed service tokens.
Restrict callers with resource policies or security groups scoped to the expected source.

rules.title: Weak authentication on exposed component
rules.description: An internet-facing component relies on weak authentication (basic auth or static API keys), or the identity provider does not enforce multi-factor authentication, making credential theft and replay practical.
remediation: Replace basic auth and static API keys with short-lived tokens (OAuth 2.0 / OIDC).
Enforce MFA in the identity provider, at minimum for privileged and administrative users.

rules.title: Unencrypted data flow across trust boundary
rules.description: Data crosses a trust boundary over an unencrypted channel and can be modified in transit by an on-path attacker.
remediation: Use TLS 1.2+ for every flow that crosses a trust boundary.
Enforce HTTPS-only listeners and redirect plain HTTP at the edge.

rules.title: Missing input validation
rules.description: An application component does not validate input, exposing it to injection and parameter tampering.
remediation: Validate all input against an allow-list schema at the trust boundary (e.g. Joi, API Gateway request validation).
Use parameterised queries and context-aware output encoding.

rules.title: Unscanned third-party dependencies
rules.description: The component's build pipeline does not scan third-party dependencies, so a compromised or vulnerable package can tamper with application behaviour.
remediation: Add software composition analysis to CI (npm audit, Snyk, Dependabot) with a failing security gate.
Pin dependency versions with a lockfile and verify package integrity.

rules.title: No audit logging on application component
rules.description: An application component does not log security-relevant actions, so users or attackers can deny having performed them.
remediation: Log authentication events, authorisation failures and state-changing actions with actor identity and timestamp.
Ship logs to a central, append-only store (e.g. CloudWatch Logs with restricted delete permissions).

rules.title: No access logging on sensitive data store
rules.description: A data store holding confidential or restricted data does not record access, so reads and changes cannot be attributed.
remediation: Enable data-plane access logging (e.g. S3 server access logs, CloudTrail data events, DynamoDB stream auditing).
Retain access logs for the period required by your compliance obligations.

rules.title: No centralised security monitoring
rules.description: The architecture has no monitoring or log aggregation component, so events cannot be correlated or protected from tampering.
remediation: Add a central monitoring component (e.g. CloudTrail + CloudWatch, or a SIEM) and model it in the architecture.
Protect log integrity with log-file validation and a separate logging account.

rules.title: Sensitive data store not encrypted at rest
rules.description: A data store holding confidential or restricted data is not encrypted at rest, exposing data if storage media, snapshots or backups are accessed.
remediation: Enable encryption at rest with KMS-managed keys (SSE-KMS for S3, KMS encryption for DynamoDB/RDS).
Restrict kms:Decrypt to the roles that need it.

rules.title: Sensitive data transmitted in cleartext
rules.description: A data flow carrying confidential or restricted data is unencrypted and can be read by anyone able to observe the channel.
remediation: Encrypt the flow with TLS 1.2+, including flows inside the VPC when they carry sensitive data.
Consider field-level encryption for the most sensitive attributes.

rules.title: Non-public data store exposed to the internet
rules.description: A data store that does not hold exclusively public data is reachable from the internet — the classic misconfigured-bucket exposure.
remediation: Block public access (S3 Block Public Access at account level) and serve content only through an authenticated path.
Place data stores in private subnets with no internet route.

rules.title: No rate limiting on exposed component
rules.description: An internet-facing component does not rate-limit requests, so it can be exhausted by request floods or brute-force traffic.
remediation: Configure throttling (API Gateway usage plans / stage throttling) and per-client quotas.
Add WAF rate-based rules for unauthenticated endpoints.

rules.title: No edge protection for internet-facing system
rules.description: The system is internet-facing but no edge component or API layer has a web application firewall, leaving it exposed to volumetric and application-layer attacks.
remediation: Front the system with CloudFront and AWS WAF (managed rule groups) and enable AWS Shield.
Model the edge component explicitly with waf: true once in place.

rules.title: Single point of failure in stateful component
rules.description: A database, queue or cache has no redundancy, so a single failure or targeted attack makes dependent services unavailable.
remediation: Deploy across multiple Availability Zones or use a managed service with built-in replication.
Define and test backup and restore procedures.

rules.title: Over-permissive execution role
rules.description: A compute component's execution role is not scoped to least privilege, so a compromise of the component grants broad access to other resources.
remediation: Scope IAM execution roles to specific actions and resource ARNs; avoid wildcards.
Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate policies from observed access.

rules.title: Authentication without authorisation
rules.description: The component authenticates callers but does not enforce object- or function-level authorisation, so any authenticated user can reach other users' data or privileged functions.
remediation: Enforce authorisation checks on every request, server-side, against the resource owner and role.
Deny by default and centralise access-control logic.

rules.title: Component runs with elevated privileges
rules.description: The component runs as root or in a privileged container, so any code-execution flaw yields full control of the host or runtime.
remediation: Run as a non-root user and drop all Linux capabilities not explicitly required.
Disable privileged mode in task/pod definitions.
